PhD
Doctoral programme
The exact structure of your doctoral programme is determined in consultation with your supervisors at your faculty. During the doctoral programme, you will work on your research and, in many cases, also teach.
What a Doctoral programme generally looks like
A Doctoral programme has set elements for the beginning, middle and end.
The start of your Doctoral programme
In consultation with your supervisor(s):
Define your research objective and draw up a research plan
Draft a Training and Supervision Plan (OBP) with your supervisor. This records matters such as research design, timeline, teaching, training, supervision, career orientation, and budget
Collecting research results
You collect your results
You will often write one or two draft chapters of your thesis
Writing and final phase
You write your thesis
Defending your thesis (the doctoral defence) is the official completion of your PhD track
Facilities and support
UvA offers various facilities and resources you can consult for information and help, such as:
Training and courses, financial support, and assistance with practical matters
Opportunities to meet other PhD candidates and to develop your creative or sporting side
Contact points and provisions for PhD candidates who experience stress, mental health issues or unwanted behaviour during their PhD (check with your supervisor which facilities apply to you, as it may differ per type of PhD programme)
Representation of PhD candidates
PhD candidates are represented by the Central PhD Council (CPC). The CPC consists of delegates from the faculty PhD councils. They identify issues and discuss them with the Executive Board.
